description: After the Landing is an interactive educational website that explores the human-made objects and equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions. It uncovers the stories behind these forgotten objects, explaining their origins, purposes, they were part of. Through engaging visuals, interactive features, and informative content, our project aims to raise awareness about the history of space exploration and the lasting traces of human presence beyond Earth.
summary: "Abandoned but not Forgotten" is an educational digital archive that explores the history and legacy of space exploration. Our project documents the spacecraft, rovers, instruments, and other equipment left behind during missions to the Moon and Mars. It features 77 catalog entries, including 27 Moon entries and 50 Mars entries, covering NASA missions as well as Soviet and Chinese exploration. Through historical information, NASA images, interactive exploration, location directories, and educational content, visitors can discover where these objects were deployed and what they contributed to scientific progress. The project addresses the challenge of preserving the stories of space exploration by bringing forgotten hardware and its discoveries into one accessible platform. Its purpose is to inspire curiosity, improve space-science awareness, and help the next generation understand that even when a mission ends, its scientific contributions continue to shape our understanding of the universe.
details:
Abandoned but not Forgotten – After the Landing is an interactive educational archive designed to preserve and explore the history of space exploration. Our project focuses on human-made spacecraft, rovers, scientific instruments, and other equipment left on the Moon and Mars after space missions.

The website organizes information into two main collections: a 27-entry Moon catalog and a 50-entry Mars catalog, making a total of 77 catalog entries. Visitors can explore historical missions, discover the stories behind different space artifacts, view NASA images, and access location directories supported by NASA references. The website also includes an interactive MCQ section to make learning more engaging.

Our project aims to make space exploration history accessible and interesting, especially for students, educators, and people interested in astronomy and science. It highlights how equipment left behind continues to represent important scientific achievements and discoveries.

What makes our project creative is its storytelling approach. Instead of focusing only on successful landings and active missions, we bring attention to the forgotten hardware and its lasting scientific contributions. We also considered historical accuracy, reliable sources, image credits, educational value, accessibility, and clear presentation while organizing the information.
